structural_criterion.statement: An amidine/guanidine carbon (C bearing a C=N double bond) excludes its attached amino nitrogens' N-H from reactive_amine_hydrogen_count UNLESS that carbon's own imine (=N) nitrogen itself bears a cyanamide (nitrile-carbon) substituent -- the specific N#C-N=C(NH2)(NH2) motif that structurally defines dicyandiamide (cyanoguanidine, CAS 461-58-5). In that narrow case the terminal amino N-H's are counted normally; the exemption does not apply to a nitrile anywhere else in the molecule, only to one bonded directly to the guanidine carbon's own imine nitrogen.
structural_criterion.why_this_is_the_correct_boundary: R-N02's exclusion is premised on symmetric, three-nitrogen 'Y-delocalized' resonance stabilizing guanidinium-type cations, which makes the neutral N-H non-nucleophilic (guanidine conjugate-acid pKaH = 13.6; delocalization-stabilized superbase). A cyano substituent on the imine nitrogen is a strong pi-acceptor that competes for that same electron density, collapsing the symmetric resonance the exclusion depends on: cyanoguanidine's conjugate-acid pKaH is reported at only ~0.7 (predicted; chembk.com CAS 461-58-5 listing), a >12 log-unit basicity collapse versus guanidine. Mechanistically, Fedtke, Domaratius & Walter, 'Curing of epoxy resins with dicyandiamide,' Polymer Bulletin 31:429-435 (1993), DOI 10.1007/BF00329879, show dicyandiamide's terminal amino nitrogens nucleophilically ring-open a glycidyl-ether epoxide model compound to form N-alkyl adducts -- direct evidence those N-H's are reactive, not resonance-inert. Patent WO1993010168A1 (1993) states dicyandiamide has a defined functionality of four. Pure alkyl/aryl/H-substituted guanidines (guanidine itself, DPG CAS 102-06-7, DOTG CAS 97-39-2, biguanide) carry no such substituent, retain the full symmetric resonance, and are unaffected: they stay 0.
